By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 09:01.

According to recent reports, with the serious injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, PSG are expected to look to strengthen in the January transfer window. An ideal profile has been identified and two targets have already been ruled out.

It is a double blow for PSG. Desire Doue has joined Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in the treatment room, probably until the end of the season, as both Paris attackers have suffered cruciate ligament ruptures.

While the signing of an attacker was already being considered after the Georgian's injury, it now seems necessary with the French player's, which was added this weekend.

According to Le Parisien, the decision-makers at the capital club are nevertheless split between trusting the current squad and not compromising the rest of the season.

Luis Enrique does have solutions to cover for these two notable absences with Senny Mayulu, Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts or Quentin Ndjantou.

Luis Campos will be attentive to opportunities in January, with a specific player profile in mind: a versatile attacking player, more of a winger than a centre-forward. To match Luis Enrique's expectations, he will need to be comfortable in tight spaces, capable of provoking and dominating his opponent one-on-one.

Recent findings suggest that the same source indicates that Eli Junior Kroupi and Paris Brunner, who are nevertheless two highly sought-after gems, do not have the profile PSG are looking for this January. They are therefore two options to be set aside. Finding the ideal player will be no easy task in the January transfer window, as the substantial European clubs will not be inclined to part with an important player mid-season.

Moreover, Paris no longer wish to overpay for their signings, despite this extraordinary situation. The Paris hierarchy therefore have six weeks before the January transfer window opens to deepen their search and potentially find the perfect player. Between now and January 2027, Luis Enrique, for his part, will be able to assess his attacking resources and try to maintain a good level of performance.

  • The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but fresh manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

According to recent reports, 'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always demonstrated how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

It has been revealed that 'And I've always said the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club states "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a fresh contract so I think that from their side demonstrates that they want me to stay.

'As I mentioned there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

Sources indicate that the club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

Sources indicate that united presently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he stated.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

His post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

Industry observers note that 'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

It has been revealed that 'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:13.

European football returns to the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday evening, when Arsenal welcome a Borussia Dortmund side just one point below them in the Champions League rankings.

The Gunners have navigated their opening four matches unbeaten to collect 10 points and sit third in the table, while Niko Kovac's side have lost one and won three in the continent's top tier so far to lie 12th.

Here, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Industry observers note that arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund is scheduled for an 8pm kickoff on Tuesday, November 24.

Another six matches will commence at the same time, including Manchester City vs. Napoli and Real Madrid vs. PSV Eindhoven.

Arsenal are hosting Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, where Mikel Arteta's men have won each of their first six games in all tournaments this season, conceding just two goals in the process.

BVB last visited Arsenal's home turf in 2014, when Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez propelled the Gunners to a 2-0 group-stage victory.

In a recent development, arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund will not be shown on terrestrial television in the UK; instead, the fixture will be broadcast on Amazon Prime Video.

Fans with an Amazon Prime Video subscription can watch the game on a variety of devices, such as via the TV app, phones, computers and games consoles.

Amazon Prime Video costs £8.99 a month for the full Amazon Prime package, or £7.99 a month for just Amazon Prime Video, although the latter is only available to select accounts.

Highlights of the match will be made available on the Amazon Prime and TNT Sports YouTube channels shortly after full time, as well as the official Arsenal account.

The @primevideosport X account will also post short clips of key moments as and when they happen.

It has been revealed that top spot in the Champions League table is within Arsenal's reach, as the third-placed Gunners are just two points behind Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, the latter of whom do not take to the field until Wednesday vs. Roma.

Arteta's men will therefore rise to first for at least 24 hours if they win and Real Madrid lose to PSV, or if they triumph, Los Blancos draw and Arsenal also make up a -1 goal difference to Jose Mourinho's side.

The Gunners could also equal two Champions League records, as they are a win or draw away from matching their longest-ever run of unbeaten group stage/league phase games (17) and could also draw level with Liverpool's English record of 13 consecutive group stage/league phase wins at home.

On the other hand, Dortmund are capable of rising into the top eight automatic qualification places with a shock win in North London, but head coach Kovac has only won one of his previous five Champions League matches against an English club; a 7-2 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur with Bayern Munich in 2019.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rangers and Celtic are unable to compete with European clubs when it comes to signing Scottish players, and it is becoming a concern.
  • The Old Firm rivals' difficulties in recent seasons have added to the concerns about a lack of top players coming through the ranks at Scotland's biggest clubs.
  • This comes after Rangers' 2-1 win against Motherwell saw the first time in history that neither side had named a Scottish player in the starting XI of a SPFL game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers and Celtic are unable to compete with European clubs when it comes to signing Scottish players, and it is becoming a concern.

The Old Firm rivals' difficulties in recent seasons have added to the concerns about a lack of top players coming through the ranks at Scotland's biggest clubs.

This comes after Rangers' 2-1 win against Motherwell saw the first time in history that neither side had named a Scottish player in the starting XI of a SPFL game.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that the decline of Rangers and Celtic in recent years highlights the problem Scottish football is facing.

Alongside the concern about the lack of talent coming through, a number of Scottish players have also sought moves abroad, rather than joining one of the Old Firm clubs.

The likes of Lewis Ferguson, Robbie Ure and Aaron Hickey have moved abroad in recent years, while Scott McTominay and John McGinn are playing at the top level.

Brown warned Football Insider on 24 November that Scottish football is facing a serious problem regarding the level of players coming through their academy systems.

Sebastien Pogocnoli's national team side are also facing a decline given the low number of top emerging talents, and something must be done to resolve it.

Rangers and Celtic have also been mentioned as potential reasons, with neither club able to compete at their previous levels, and therefore missing out to bigger clubs.

"Like it or not, a lot of whether Scottish football is doing well depends on Rangers and Celtic," Brown told Football Insider.

"If they're at their best, they're competing in Europe, then players are going to want to go and play for them, but at the moment they're missing out on those players.

"That's part of the problem, because their decline means they're not luring the best Scottish players to come and play in Scotland.

Sources indicate that "What you have to look at is; who are the best Scottish players right now? You'd probably say Scott McTominay and John McGinn, but neither of them are playing in Scotland.

"Historically, you'd always think that Rangers and Celtic can compete to sign the best Scottish players, but that's not the case any more.

"They don't have the finances to beat some of the top European clubs, and they're not playing at a high enough level to be a draw in that respect, so that is a problem.

"The best players coming through in Scotland are having to move abroad to further their careers, we've seen that a lot recently and that's never a good sign for the state of the SPFL.".

Much of the concern surrounding top Scottish clubs' signing younger domestic players comes down to the fees they are willing to spend on rival players.

Instead, Brown told Football Insider during the summer that Rangers have to be clever with their recruitment, with scouts working across Europe to identify top young players.

The Ibrox club were scouring areas including Scandanavia and Eastern Europe for talent, having had success when recruiting from there in the past.

Interestingly enough, Rangers CEO Andrew Cavenagh explained during the summer that the club would operate with a "Scottish bias" as part of fresh-look transfer intends.

Lawrence Shankland, James Penrice and Ross McCrorie then all completed moves to Ibrox, but the debate still lingers about the quality of talent coming through.

By Oliver Thomas | 23 Nov 2026 09:20.

Gameweek five in the Champions League sees Manchester City and Napoli square off in the League Phase.

These two teams suffered contrasting results in the previous round of fixtures, and here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into to their latest encounter.

Sources indicate that man City vs. Napoli will kick off at 20:00 UK time on Tuesday night.

This contest is one of nine taking place on the same evening, with Man City’s English rivals Arsenal among those also in action at home to Borussia Dortmund.

This Champions League match will take place at Man City’s home the Etihad Stadium, which now holds a capacity of 61,470 spectators following a recent expansion.

Man City have lost only two of their last 27 home fixtures in the group stage/League Phase of the Champions League (W22 D3), though one of those was earlier this season against holders Paris Saint-Germain (4-2).

Recent findings suggest that man City vs. Napoli will be shown live on TNT Sports 1 or TNT Sports Ultimate for viewers in the UK.

Fans with the TNT Sports package through their TV provider can watch this game on Sky Go and Virgin TV Go, while this fixture will also be streamed live on Amazon Prime Video in the UK, and on CBS on Paramount+ in the USA.

Match highlights of Man City vs. Napoli will be available on Amazon Prime Video, TNT Sports and via BBC Sport’s dedicated UEFA Champions League Match of the Day show which you can watch live or stream on BBC iPlayer.

You can also view this match on the TNT Sports YouTube channel and both clubs' official YouTube accounts.

At the halfway stage in the League Phase, Man City sit seventh in the 36-team standings after accumulating nine points from their opening four matches.

Enzo Maresca’s side will realistically need at least a couple more victories to ensure they finish inside the top eight and secure automatic qualification for the last 16, rather than slip into the playoffs.

The Citizens have won each of their last three Champions League meetings with Napoli, most recently winning 2-0 on home soil in the League Phase of last season’s competition courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku.

Napoli will therefore be out for revenge when they make the trip back to the blue side of Manchester, while Wednesday’s fixture also marks the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne, whose first comeback to the Etihad was cut short.

Indeed, he was the unfortunate one sacrificed after just 21 minutes following a red card for Giovanni Di Lorenzo in Napoli's 2-0 defeat last season.

The Italian club have won one and lost three of their opening four UCL games this term, suffering a disappointing 4-1 defeat at Porto on November 4, and currently sit down in 27th place in the table, six points behind the top eight.

While Napoli enter this contest on the back of a narrow 1-0 home win over Torino in Serie A on Saturday, courtesy of a Scott McTominay goal, Man City were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham in the Premier League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League confirmed updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The new dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool right now have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

Industry observers note that luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' stated De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

In a recent development, asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

It has been revealed that you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

Recent findings suggest that there has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

It has been revealed that spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

Recent findings suggest that belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' mentioned Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

It has been revealed that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

In a recent development, christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a latest contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

“I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract currently set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Sources indicate that liverpool, it has to be remarked, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Industry observers note that falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The massive issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

In a recent development, the Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under newly introduced boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 23 Nov 2026 09:36.

Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri will reunite with his parent club when Borussia Dortmund take on the Premier League champions in Tuesday's Champions League clash at the Emirates Stadium.

The 19-year-old joined the German giants on a season-long loan during the final hours of the summer transfer window, but he is yet to find his best form under Niko Kovac.

Nwaneri has only provided one assist and no goals from his first 13 appearances in a Dortmund shirt across all competitions, that contribution coming on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim.

Since then, the 2007-born playmaker has only started four Bundesliga matches, and he is still waiting to make a first XI in the Champions League, being restricted to 87 minutes across four substitute outings.

Nwaneri was also given just a one-minute run-out in the weekend's 1-0 Bundesliga win over Borussia Monchengladbach, but he may be given the chance to strut his stuff against his boyhood team.

Champions League rules permit loan players to face their parent clubs in the Champions League, so Nwaneri will be able to feature in Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Unlike in the Premier League and other domestic competitions in England, where loan players cannot take on parent teams without special dispensation, there are no such restrictions outlined in the Champions League rules and regulations.

However, if Nwaneri was to return to Arsenal in January, the England Under-21 international would not be able to feature for the Premier League champions for the remainder of the tournament.

Article 30.05 of UEFA's Champions League regulations states that 'A player may not play in the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League or UEFA Conference League for more than one club in a single season', but Arsenal are not expected to bring Nwaneri back to North London over the winter.

The teenager has scored 10 goals and set up two more in 51 Arsenal games since making his debut against Brentford in September 2022, when he became the Premier League's youngest player of all time.

Goal Bayern Munich. Philippe Coutinho. 2-8.

Loan players making decisive contributions against parent clubs in the Champions League has been a semi-regular occurrence, the most notable example being Philippe Coutinho in 2020.

The then-Barcelona playmaker was shipped out to Bayern Munich and reunited with La Blaugrana in the quarter-finals of the 2019-20 edition, when he incredibly scored twice in an 8-2 annihilation.

Sixteen years prior, Fernando Morientes - on loan at Monaco from Real Madrid - scored in both legs of the quarter-final against Los Blancos, helping Les Monegasques knock out his parent team on away goals before they lost to Porto in the final.

Sources indicate that real were also stung by James Rodriguez in the 2017-18 semi-finals vs. Bayern Munich, but the Colombian's goal - which he refused to celebrate - was not enough to prevent Los Blancos advancing 4-3 on aggregate.

The 2013-14 semi-finals saw Thibaut Courtois play a crucial role in Atletico Madrid's success against parent club Chelsea, who tried to force Los Rojiblancos to pay them £2.5m for each game the Belgian goalkeeper played against them, only for UEFA to rule the terms null, void and unenforceable.

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

It has been revealed that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

According to recent reports, the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

In a recent development, carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Industry observers note that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In a recent development, in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager remarked. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Industry observers note that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

According to recent reports, united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and rapidly.

Industry observers note that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick stated: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chris Sutton has stated he can ‘only see one result’ from Liverpool’s showdown against Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

The home side go into the fixture 10 points and 14 places ahead of their arch-rivals, for whom this is a first game in charge for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

The Reds’ home record in the Premier League so far this season has been poor, with just one win from five, but victory today would see them close to within one point of third-placed Manchester City.

In his weekly Premier League column for BBC Sport, Sutton voiced his belief that the visitors won’t have any ‘upcoming manager bounce’ at Anfield and has forecast Liverpool to win handsomely.

The former Chelsea striker wrote: ‘Liverpool are still a work in progress, and United have picked up some results at Anfield recently – two draws and a win in their past three visits – but I can only see one result here, and it is a home victory.

Industry observers note that ‘Pochettino will probably look to defend and play on the counterattack, and they might get some chances that way, but Liverpool are going to win. The only question is how many they will score.

According to recent reports, ‘Carrick began by beating Manchester City and Arsenal in his first two games in January. Pochettino might start by being on the wrong end of a pummelling.’.

Sutton has predicted a resounding 4-0 win for Liverpool, matching the scoreline from this fixture in April 2022.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

In a recent development, considering the form and league positions of the teams, objectively the Reds ought to go into this game as clear favourites. When fifth plays host to second from bottom in the Premier League, the former would naturally be expected to win.

However, the pundit referenced Man United’s good record at Anfield since the famous 7-0 drubbing in March 2023, and Liverpool were also widely expected to win on a couple of those occasions.

Pochettino has never lost his first match at any of the five clubs he’s previously managed, and Reds fans might naturally be wary that the players who effectively downed tools under Michael Carrick will suddenly have a spring in their step today.

The good news for Iraola is that he has a mostly fully-fit squad, with Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai overcoming minor challenges over the past couple of weeks and Ryan Gravenberch available once more, and there were no fresh injury casualties over the international window.

According to recent reports, the Liverpool head coach has had a reasonably good start to his reign but is still waiting on a genuine ‘statement’ victory. That would change if Sutton’s emphatic prediction comes to light, but we’re sure that every Kopite would gladly take a win by any means against our biggest rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 09:53.

Watford play host to Blackburn Rovers on Wednesday night searching for yet another permanent head coach after the sacking of Alessio Dionisi.

At a time when the Hornets sit in 21st position in the Championship table, Rovers make the trip to Vicarage Road sitting among the mid-table places.

Whenever a new manager arrives at Watford, there is always an inevitability that his stay at Vicarage Road will be a short one.

A 10th defeat across 18 matches in all competitions led to Dionisi being dismissed after Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

With Watford having earned four points from games against Lincoln City and Middlesbrough before the international break, it feels that the Italian could have been provided with more time in the dugout.

Instead, the Pozzo Family has decided to act with Watford ending the weekend sitting four points above the relegation zone.

On a positive note, Watford are unbeaten in their last three games at Vicarage Road, collecting seven points in the process, while they have only conceded nine goals in eight home league fixtures during 2026-27.

As for Blackburn, they responded to Tony Mowbray stepping down from his first-team duties with a 2-2 draw at rivals Burnley on Sunday.

Having twice come from behind, Rovers will be satisfied with a deserved share of the spoils at Turf Moor, a result that keeps them 11 points above the relegation zone despite being viewed as one of the favourites for the drop in the summer.

Furthermore, 17 points have been accumulated from their last 10 games, emphasising that they could still challenge for a top-eight spot this campaign.

However, Blackburn remain with just one away win this campaign, only recording seven points from eight matches while shipping 15 goals.

Blackburn Rovers Championship form:.

While the Watford lineup and formation is difficult to predict, personnel changes are expected after the drab performance at Sheffield United.

Hector Kyprianou, Rocco Vata and Luca Kjerrumgaard are all options in midfield and attack.

Three Watford players - Mattie Pollock, Kevin Keben and Martin Payero - are all one yellow card away from a one-match ban.

With Tom Atcheson expected to miss out with the head injury that he sustained at Burnley, Blackburn could switch to a back four.

Jayden Fevrier was introduced as an early substitute at Turf Moor before he was replaced by Ryoya Morishita 62 minutes later, so the latter could get the nod here.

Second-choice goalkeeper Aynsley Pears will remain between the sticks, a consequence of Balasz Toth being ruled out until January with a hand injury.

Watford possible starting lineup:.

Ravaglia; Traore, Coulibaly, Pollock, Keben, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou; Vata, Kjerrumgaard, Mavididi.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Pears; Beyuku, McLoughlin, Carter, Pickering; Montgomery, Baradji; Morishita, Cantwell, Afolayan; Gudjohnsen.

Sources indicate that although both of these teams are without a permanent manager in charge, Blackburn are far more settled than Watford. With that in mind, we are backing the visitors to earn a deserved victory at Vicarage Road, keeping themselves within touching distance of the playoffs in the process.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase. Because most stars are thought to host orbiting companions (such as planets, other stars or black holes), interesting interactions can happen as the giant host expands. The most striking of these occur when a companion star is engulfed by a giant: astronomers refer to this as the common-envelope phase1. Despite theoretical expectations that common envelopes should be widespread in stellar evolution, they have been extraordinarily difficult to observe. Writing in Nature, however, Karambelkar et al.2 report the first direct detection of a star inside a giant star.

Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund in their latest Champions League clash on Tuesday night.

The Gunners dropped European points for the second time this season at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyokeres broke the deadlock in the 10th minute with a stunning strike from long range as he caught Gregor Kobel off his line.

Max Beier levelled the score just after the break and the German side held on for a priceless point away to the English champions.

Italian official Maurizio Mariani was involved in some controversy as the man in the middle on the night.

Football Insider have picked out three decisions that Mariani should have done better with during the Champions League clash.

Tempers flared slightly in the 53rd minute as Hincapie and Ryerson came together and the Arsenal defender ended up in a heap on the floor.

Ryerson was not best pleased with whatever went on, as Mariani ignored the incident, but replays showed that Hincapie had feigned injury to get the Dortmund man booked, or maybe even sent off.

His hand had slightly touched the Gunners' defender's face, but Hincapie went down way too theatrically, and should have been sanctioned for simulation by the letter of the law.

Dortmund's players were adamant that they deserved a penalty in the second half after Gyokeres jumped to clear from their corner.

The Arsenal goalscorer clearly used his arm to block the ball while challenging, even if he did not mean to.

Mariani failed to spot the offence and so did the VAR officials, despite it looking like a clear spot-kick as he moved his arm away from his body.

It was Dortmund's turn to get away with a handball offence not long after, although this one was not in the area.

The former Man United midfielder challenged Eberechi Eze in the 78th minute before throwing his arm towards the ball to stop the Gunners' playmaker advancing.

Mariani rightfully gave the hosts a free kick, but somehow decided not to book the Austrian star despite it clearly being a yellow card offence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026.

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title.

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched.

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021.

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

Man City were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium in their latest disappointing performance under Enzo Maresca.

City were forced to come from behind twice against Serie A opposition as they slipped to sixth in the Champions League standings.

Former Man United man Rasmus Hojlund put the visitors ahead shortly before the hour mark as he slipped the ball under Gianluigi Donnarumma from close range.

Ayyoub Bouaddi levelled with his first City goal in the 67th minute before Noa Lang put the visitors ahead.

Rayan Cherki's late strike rescued a point for City as several surprise flashpoints occurred throughout.

Football Insider have picked out four moments that City fans might have missed during the Etihad Stadium clash.

Man City icon De Bruyne returned to the Etihad for a second time as a player since leaving the club for Napoli in 2025.

The Belgian's legendary status was reflected before the game, as his chant rang out among home supporters shortly before kick-off.

Man City fans unveiled a tifo to honor Kevin De Bruyne 👑 pic.twitter.com/myMvwM7cca.

The City fans also unveiled a tifo to honour 'King Kev' before the game started.

De Bruyne ultimately shone on his latest return to the club before being taken off in the 75th minute.

Napoli were always a threat from set pieces and that looked to be the work of one of their coaches in particular, who constantly stood by the touchline every time they had a dead ball.

The member of away staff was pointed out by City's The Athletic reporter, Sam Lee, who also happened to catch him slipping on his backside before posting the video to X.

Oh my god https://t.co/L5pkUXO9DO pic.twitter.com/BFwD3AB6ik.

It was a lighthearted moment during a game full of tense moments in Manchester.

Hojlund has mostly impressed in Naples since the last time he played for United in the 2024-25 season, with 16 goals in 44 games on loan last term and a further four in 16 this season.

His goal will have pleased Red Devils fans, even in their current predicament, and it did look as if he mouthed the words "Manchester" while he held up one finger during the celebration.

Industry observers note that the 23-year-old admitted after the game that he had done so to insinuate that his former employers remain the best in their city, saying: "Yeah, it was some good banter, you know. There's the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United, and obviously I have a past at United.

"So that's my club, and nothing against Man City. But yeah, United is my club. It was good to score here.".

Referee Kovacs had already angered City fans when he only added two minutes on at the end of the game despite numerous goals and substitutions.

He then blew the whistle around 20 seconds before the 92nd minute passed, according to the stadium clock, which drew strong reactions from players as they surrounded him, and fans, who booed.

The TNT Sports clock was consistent with his timing, however, so it was unclear who was truly in the wrong.

The Red Devils sit 19th in the Premier League table, boasting only eight points from 11 matches, and it has been a disastrous opening to the campaign for the club.

Elsewhere, title favourites Arsenal and Manchester City were held to draws by Newcastle United and Fulham respectively, while Leeds United recorded a standout 4-1 win at Chelsea.

There were also victories for Tottenham Hotspur, Coventry City, Bournemouth and Hull City, while Sunderland held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at Villa Park.

Here, Sports Mole presents its Premier League Team of the Week for Gameweek 11 of the 2026-27 campaign, according to the data.

Sunderland goalkeeper Roefs was in excellent form in his side's goalless draw against Villa, coming up with eight saves, playing a vital role in the Black Cats claiming a point.

Porro provided the assist for Luca Williams-Barnett to send Tottenham ahead in the clash with Ipswich Town, and his use of the ball throughout the contest was excellent, with the right-back showing his Spain performance level in this contest.

Silva was exceptional in the heart of the Bournemouth defence against Nottingham Forest, winning seven aerial duels and making four tackles, while his pass success rate was 85%.

In just his third Premier League appearance of the season, Senesi was excellent against Ipswich, winning two aerial duels, while his pass success rate was up at 91%.

Kerkez has found it difficult to show his best form since arriving at Liverpool, but he put in a dominant performance against Man United on Sunday to help Andoni Iraola's side claim a clean sheet, while he was also a threat going the other way.

Wirtz was in inspired form against Man United, with the Germany international scoring and providing an assist in Liverpool's four-goal success; this was much more like it from the playmaker, who has largely been criticised since arriving in English football.

Okafor put in an exceptional performance to help Leeds win 4-1 at Chelsea on Saturday, scoring twice in the incredible success for Daniel Farke's side.

In a recent development, what a performance from the 18-year-old; Ngumoha scored once and also provided an assist in Liverpool's 4-0 win over Man United. Red Devils defender Diogo Dalot will be glad that he does not have to face the incredible teenager every week.

Stoke City vs Millwall - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:53.
  • Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.
  • At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil returns to one of his former clubs, with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:53.

Stoke City square off against Millwall on Wednesday night looking for the win that would keep the club in the automatic promotion spots of the Championship table.

At a time when the Potters are in second position, Alex Neil returns to one of his former clubs, with the Lions beginning the week in 16th place.

The November international break came at the wrong time for Stoke, who have established themselves as contenders for promotion to the Premier League.

Nevertheless, Mark Robins's side returned on Saturday with a 1-0 win over then-leaders Birmingham City, making it 10 victories from their last 13 games in the Championship.

Rather incredibly, Stoke have accumulated 16 points from their last six games without scoring more than twice in a single match.

Just two goals have been conceded during that period, while Stoke have four clean sheets from their most recent six games at the bet365 Stadium, including their last three.

Despite starting the campaign with three successive defeats, no team in the Championship has won more games (10) than Stoke in 2026-27.

Meanwhile, Neil returns to the bet365 Stadium with Millwall having lost five of their most recent seven games.

Three successive defeats, the latest a 1-0 home loss to Queens Park Rangers after Zak Sturge was sent off in the 15th minute, have left the Scot fighting to keep his job at The Den.

Millwall, who reached the playoffs last season, are nine points adrift of eighth spot, and defeat to Stoke would leave the East London outfit cut adrift from the mid-table places.

As well as losing five of their eight away matches this campaign, Millwall have conceded 18 goals on their travels, the joint-second worst defensive record in such fixtures in the division.

Stoke could make at least three changes, a consequence of Luca Bombino's red card against Birmingham and Djibril Soumare and George Hirst both picking up injuries in the same game.

Eric-Junior Bocat should start at left wing-back, Svante Ingelsson is in line to feature in midfield should Ethan Galbraith not return after illness, and Sam Gallagher could get the nod ahead of Robert Bozenik in attack.

Million Manhoef may also start on one of the flanks should Robins wish to introduce further fresh legs.

Meanwhile, Alfie Doughty could be introduced as a straight replacement for suspended Millwall defender Zak Sturge.

With the Lions having failed to score in three successive matches, Zak Lovelace and Mihailo Ivanovic will feel they are in contention to start in the final third.

Luke Cundle, Romain Esse and Josh Coburn will all be assessed after missing the QPR defeat on Saturday.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Ingelsson, McGlynn, Bocat; Devenny, Gallagher, Bae.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lovelace; Ivanovic.

While this contest could prove to be closer than many are anticipating, it is difficult to back against a Stoke side that have kept clean sheets in their last three home games, especially against a Millwall team that have conceded 18 goals on the road and are without the suspended Zak Sturge. With that in mind, we are predicting a narrow win for the Potters.

Industry News: Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have unveiled they're expecting their first child together.
  • The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:18 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 22 November 2026.

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have unveiled they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby.

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'.

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside swiftly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

According to recent reports, this season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test.

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino.

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 10:35, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 10:37.

Francesco Pio Esposito was in sensational form on Sunday, scoring a hat-trick in Inter Milan's 4-4 draw with Atalanta BC in Serie A.

The 21-year-old has now netted seven times and registered two assists in 14 appearances for Inter during the 2026-27 campaign, and there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future at San Siro.

Manchester United allegedly recently scouted the 6ft 3in striker, with the Red Devils planning to bring in a new forward next year.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with Esposito, who has 18 goals and nine assists in 64 appearances for Inter in all competitions.

As expected, the form of the Italy international against Atalanta drew huge praise from the Italian media.

What did the Italian media say about Esposito performance?

Corriere dello Sport handed Esposito an overall performance rating of 8/10 and branded the striker "unstoppable" for his excellent display.

Tuttosport called the striker "Super Pio" and focused on his contribution to Inter's attacking display, but it was still not enough to secure his side all three points.

Tuttomercatoweb said "Esposito like Haaland" during their post-match piece, with the Inter forward being compared to Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland.

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia gave him Inter's highest rating of 8/10.

Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury problems are expected to put Man United in the market for a fresh striker in January, but they might have to wait until the end of the campaign to bring in a big-name player in that area of the field.

Inter are noted to value Esposito in the region of £84m, but that could prove to be a bargain if he continues to develop throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

Esposito has scored 10 times in 15 appearances for Italy, and he seemingly has the skill set to be a huge success in the Premier League.

Man United may bring in an experienced option, most likely on loan, during the January market, before launching a big-money move for Esposito next summer, providing that they are able to hold off the threat of Premier League relegation.

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has spoken about Gerry Cardinale’s presence, as well as the challenge Frosinone will present.

Milan are hoping to jump back into the top four by beating Frosinone, after Como overtook them with their win on Saturday. However, it will not be a straightforward task against a side that have surprised many upon their return to Serie A, and with a point they would go back above Juventus.

How notable is constant presence of Cardinale?

  • The league phase of the Champions League continues this week as the 36 teams head into matchday five looking for the win that could prove decisive in their quest to progress through to the knockout stages.
  • Arsenal's showdown with Borussia Dortmund is arguably the pick of the matches, with those teams sitting at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga tables.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 23 Nov 2026 10:53.

The league phase of the Champions League continues this week as the 36 teams head into matchday five looking for the win that could prove decisive in their quest to progress through to the knockout stages.

Arsenal's showdown with Borussia Dortmund is arguably the pick of the matches, with those teams sitting at the top of the Premier League and Bundesliga tables.

Nevertheless, with all of the favourites for the competition being kept apart on this particular matchday, they will view it as an opportunity to edge closer to making the top eight.

As highlighted by Sports Mole, there are just four players serving suspensions ahead of matchday five.

Fresh off the back of a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Manchester United make the trip to Sporting Lisbon without Matheus Cunha.

Having scored what proved to be the winner in a thrilling contest with Roma, Cunha received a second yellow card for a needless challenge during the closing stages.

Meanwhile, Man City will face Napoli at the Etihad Stadium with the visitors being unable to select defender Rafa Marin.

He was dismissed for denying a goalscoring opportunity when Porto had the chance to move 4-1 up in Portugal.

As for AEK Athens, Aboubakary Koita is unavailable for their match against Como due to the red card that he was given versus Real Madrid.

Koita was handed a red card after the final whistle for a prolonged confrontation with the officials.

Sabah defender Aden McCarthy is the fourth player to miss the MD5 for his dismissal in the 4-1 defeat to Viking FK.

He now misses the home fixture against La Liga champions Barcelona.

Although Koita and McCarthy will miss matches this week, UEFA are currently indicating that an extra game may be added to their suspensions in due course.

Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1267 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts noted enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren.

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time.

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

It has been revealed that away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

In a recent development, the 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

Industry observers note that he wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

According to recent reports, even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal.

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

It has been revealed that playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

It has been revealed that now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Industry observers note that sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

It has been revealed that the directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

Industry observers note that A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they highlighted themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a fresh thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

Sources indicate that they are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

Industry observers note that CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.
